notes: Inverse redesign: the winning candidate (structurally amine_MDEA) is now hidden behind an oracle instead of disclosed, to avoid a label leak. Five stacked traps. (1) Solvation: bare tblite is gas-phase by default; only narrative 'dissolved in water' context is given, no explicit computational instruction, and the oracle's own environment parameter must also be set to water. (2) Direction: the graded quantity is regeneration energy (least energy to REVERSE the capture reaction), not capture favorability -- regeneration energy = -capture energy, so the correct answer is the LEAST exothermic (least favorable) capture reaction, not the most. (3) Equation recall: neither governing equation is stated in problem.md (removed from earlier drafts) -- the solver must know from standard CO2-capture chemistry that an N-H amine forms a carbamate (2:1) while a tertiary/no-N-H amine forms bicarbonate instead (1:1); wrong stoichiometry breaks the whole calculation, not just the hidden candidate's. (4) Mechanism discovery: the proposed solvent's N-H status is undisclosed AND the oracle's 'classify' mode is not named in the prompt either (removed from earlier drafts) -- the solver must call 'help' first, discover 'classify' exists, then call it to learn it has no N-H bond before it can pick the bicarbonate equation; never competitive for the win either way, but a solver that assumes carbamate without querying cannot compute a defensible answer for that candidate at all. (5) HPEEDA (a real 2026 AIChE Journal molecule, SMILES NCCN(CC)CC(O)C) is bifunctional: one primary N-H site (carbamate forms here) and one already-tertiary site (protonation site), requiring correct identification of which nitrogen reacts at each step; never competitive for the win either way. Piperazine was excluded from this design entirely after authoring: it and the hidden candidate's structural identity (MDEA) sit within ~0.1-0.9 kcal/mol of each other and independent verification attempts (including 100-conformer exhaustive searches and three independently-run blind solvers) could not reliably reproduce a consistent winner between them -- both molecules have rugged enough conformational landscapes that the head-to-head comparison is not decidable at this level of theory. Without piperazine, the hidden candidate's margin over the next-closest disclosed candidate (NH3) is a robust 3.15 kcal/mol water-solvated. Water-solvated capture energies (kcal/mol, exhaustive true-minimum verification): hidden/MDEA -11.316 (least favorable, correct answer for regeneration), NH3 -14.468, MEA -17.258, HPEEDA -17.453, DEA -18.512, EDA -20.782 (most favorable capture, worst for regeneration). Vacuum (naive) capture energies: DEA 89.922, HPEEDA 91.957, hidden/MDEA 105.951, EDA 108.662, MEA 110.762, NH3 139.427 (most endothermic, naive-wrong 'winner' for regeneration under vacuum).
